checks.check: auth: session established
idempotency: both runs complete
idempotency: each run gets its own scan id
idempotency: identical input yields identical finding counts
idempotency: evidence content hashes are stable across runs
idempotency: no duplicate content_hash within a scan
checks.detail: 0 duplicated (scan_id, content_hash) pairs — known open issue, inflates finding counts

checks.check: limits: a path outside the source roots is refused
limits: a nonexistent path is refused
limits: an empty target is refused
limits: a traversal attempt is refused
limits: API still healthy after bad input
timeouts: an unreachable TLS target returns rather than hanging
timeouts: the unreachable host is not recorded as a successful probe
restart: worker process found
restart: worker killed mid-scan
restart: worker comes back
restart: the in-flight job reaches a terminal state
restart: the killed job did not produce duplicate scan rows
db outage: liveness stays up (the process is fine)
db outage: readiness drops so a load balancer drains it
db outage: readiness returns after the database comes back

scope: Covers update.md section 4's idempotency, limits/timeouts and restart/recovery on one host. It does NOT cover load and soak: that section asks for 24-72 hours against the target topology, and a run that finishes in minutes on a laptop would produce numbers resembling a capacity qualification without being one. Use scripts/soak.py and scripts/load_test.py in the real environment for that.
